claims.statement: For an ORIGINAL scalar pivot a!=0 whose exact rank-two Schur residual S has s2(S)>=L and maximum leverage mu of its two-dimensional spectral frame below 1/2, there is an ORIGINAL-coordinate cut with E2(S[I,J]) >= (1-2mu)L^4/16. Hence ||p_Q||inf < C_E2[16/(1-2mu)]^(1/8)|a|^(-1/2)L^(-1/2); if |a|>=tau L and mu<=1/4, the bound is <56.204 tau^(-1/2)L^(-1).

If s3(A)>=L, an ORIGINAL scalar pivot obeys |a|>=tau L, the exact Schur residual has top-two spectral-frame leverage <=1/8 and s3(S)<=eta L< L/4, then ||p_Q||inf < C_E2 tau^(-1/2)(1/4-eta)^(-1/2)L^(-1). At eta=1/15 the constant is <85.114 tau^(-1/2).

Let the exact Schur residual have top-three leverage <=1/16. Put g3=(4-sqrt(3))/8. If s3(S)>=beta L and s4(S)<=g3 s3(S)/16, while |a|>=tau L, then applying c2414 volume stability to a literal ORIGINAL-coordinate half-cut and reinserting the scalar square yields ||p_Q||inf <2sqrt(46/g3) tau^(-1/2) beta^(-1/2)L^(-1)<25.477 tau^(-1/2)beta^(-1/2)L^(-1).

partner_application.statement: For Q_(R,L)=LX0^2+2LRU1V1+2L/R U2V2, R>=3, ||p||inf<7.251/L. Its top-two residual frame has leverage one, so it is a complementary localized endpoint to the diffuse theorems above.
